title: I died as a mineral
hookLine: Rumi: I died as mineral and became plant, died as plant and became animal (Masnavi 3.3901ff)
carry: what did I lose by dying
tomorrow: a well-known 'Rumi' line: neither Christian, Jew nor Muslim. is it his?
last: BEFORE THE SILVER CORD · EACH ASKS ITS OWN · SEPARATE SHELVES

lines: A PERSON YOU USED TO BE.
cards: Old school photos are strange: the braces, the haircut, a person you used to be and aren't anymore. Did that kid die, or grow? Rumi asks that about the whole of a life.
In his long poem, the Masnavi, he tells his own story from the bottom up. I died as a mineral, he says, and became a plant. I died as a plant and rose to animal.
I died as an animal, and I was human.

teach.h: WHEN WAS I LESS BY DYING?
teach.b: Then comes the question that's today's line: why should I fear? When was I ever less by dying? And he doesn't stop at human.
Once more, he says, I will die as a man to rise among the angels, and pass beyond even the angel, into what no mind has pictured.
The passage closes on the Quran's words for a time of loss: "Lo! we are Allah's and lo! unto Him we are returning." Here's the teaching, in Rumi's own Muslim, Sufi world.

Each death on the ladder is a step on the road back to God, and every loss along the way has turned out to be a gain. Sufi readers take it as the soul's long journey home, not as a claim that you were once a rock.

teach.h: WHAT DID I LOSE BY DYING?
teach.b: For anyone listening with children: this poem is about death, and it is full of hope. Worth repeating: Rumi ends his ladder of deaths with the Quran's line about returning to God.

how: The 'ladder of deaths' passage from Rumi's Masnavi (book 3) is read in Sufi teaching as the soul's journey back to God; Quran 2:156, which it ends on, gives the words believers say when misfortune strikes.

games.q: a friend is graduating and says it feels like a small death, leaving who she was. what would Rumi's ladder say?
o: every death on the ladder was a step up; ask what she really loses.
endings are only losses, so she should hold on to who she was.
it means she'll be reborn as something else in a next life.
games.why: Rumi: I died as mineral and became plant... why should I fear? when was I less by dying?

practice: Find an old photo of yourself, on your phone or in a drawer, and look at it for a while. Name one thing that person had to lose for you to grow: a fear, a habit, a certainty.
Then ask Rumi's question quietly: was I less for losing it?
